LOCATION: [dynamic_management.py#L2849](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2849), [dynamic_management.py#L2893](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2893), [dynamic_management.py#L2904](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2904)  
DESCRIPTION: `ManagerEvent` is declared frozen, but its `metadata` field is a mutable dict that is shared by the producer, `_buffer`, `_all_events`, and any callback/drain consumer. Because `emit()` stores the event before invoking the callback, an observer can rewrite the already-recorded history in place. I reproduced both `e.metadata['a']=99` after `emit()` and a callback mutating `event.metadata`, and in both cases the permanent log changed retroactively. This breaks audit-log integrity for the monitoring interface.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Freeze or deep-copy `metadata` on event creation/emission, and return immutable event snapshots from the stream APIs.

SEVERITY: 0.79

LOCATION: [dynamic_management.py#L1776](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1776), [dynamic_management.py#L1793](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1793), [dynamic_management.py#L1902](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1902), [dynamic_management.py#L1941](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1941)  
DESCRIPTION: The new novelty-based stop logic is unreachable for callers using the documented `DiminishingReturnsDetector.add_round()` API. `stop()` now depends on `smoothed_novelty_rate()`, but `add_round()` has no way to supply novelty and `_novelty_rates` is never populated on that path; `novelty_rate()` silently falls back to `1.0`. I reproduced three `add_round()` calls yielding novelty rates `1.0, 1.0, 1.0`, so the cost-decoupled exhaustion signal is effectively disabled unless the caller happens to use `add_round_from_findings()`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a required or explicit `novelty_rate` input to `add_round()`, or make `stop()` raise when novelty-based stopping is enabled but novelty data was never provided.

FINDING_ID: Codex_R10_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.73  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
LOCATION: [dynamic_management.py#L2246](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2246), [dynamic_management.py#L2317](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2317)  
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor` confuses historical criticality with current criticality. When a pathology resolves, `_pathology_counts` is reset, but the old CRITICAL diagnosis stays in `_diagnoses`, and `has_critical` is defined as “any CRITICAL ever emitted.” I reproduced a kappa-stuck episode escalating to CRITICAL, followed by a healthy round; `has_critical` remained `True` after resolution. If this flag is later wired into stop or alert policy, a transient detector issue permanently taints the manager.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Track active diagnoses separately from diagnosis history, or mark diagnoses resolved and have `has_critical` reflect unresolved critical conditions only.

FINDING_ID: Codex_R10_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.68  
VERIFIED: TRUE  
LOCATION: [dynamic_management.py#L2217](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2217), [dynamic_management.py#L2314](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2314), [dynamic_management.py#L3225](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L3225)  
DESCRIPTION: Persistent detector pathologies generate duplicate diagnoses forever. Once the kappa-stuck condition holds, `record_round()` emits a new diagnosis on every later round; `DynamicManager.process_round()` then turns each one into another `STOP_CHECK` event. I reproduced six pathological rounds producing diagnosis counts `[0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]` and severities `['WARNING', 'CRITICAL', 'CRITICAL', 'CRITICAL', 'CRITICAL']`. This creates an alert storm and amplifies the already-append-only event history with repeated copies of the same condition.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Deduplicate by active pathology key, and emit only on state changes such as new, escalated, or resolved.
